bib.title: Context Embeddings for Efficient Answer Generation in RAG
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv:2407.09252v3 [cs.CL], 29 Oct 2024; ACM template placeholder 'Conference'17, July 2017, Washington, DC, USA')

question: Can multiple retrieved passages be compressed into a few context embeddings so RAG answer generation is much faster while keeping answer quality?
hypothesis: Freezing the decoder hinders use of compressed contexts; tuning the decoder jointly with the compressor gives higher effectiveness than frozen-decoder compression methods.
contributions: COCOM, a context compression method reducing long contexts to a handful of context embeddings, speeding generation with higher performance than other methods
An efficiency study of efficiency-effectiveness trade-offs at different compression rates, including compression time and memory (up to 5.69x inference time and 22x GFLOPs reduction)
Ablations on pretraining collection, pretraining, fine-tuning data and freezing or tuning the decoder

method.summary: COCOM compresses each retrieved passage independently into k=ceil(n/xi) context embeddings (last-hidden-layer states of <CTX> tokens from the same Mistral-7B LLM used as decoder; COCOM-light uses bert-base-uncased plus a learned block-wise linear projection). The LLM is LoRA-pretrained on auto-encoding and language-modeling-from-context-embeddings, then LoRA fine-tuned on a 493k multi-QA mix with 5 compressed passages as input.
method.task: open-domain / knowledge-intensive QA with RAG; context compression

datasets.name: Wikipedia-KILT chunks (kilt-128)
datasets.source: KILT Wikipedia, published as HF dataset dmrau/kilt-128

datasets.name: Multi-QA fine-tuning mix (NQ, MS MARCO, AdversarialQA, HotpotQA, WikiQA, SciQ, ASQA, FreebaseQA, SQuAD)
datasets.split: train samples; MS MARCO first 100k queries
datasets.preprocessing: filtered out queries >128 tokens and labels >64 tokens

models.name: COCOM-light
models.params: bert-base-uncased compressor + linear projection W (xi*b x d); decoder Mistral-7B
models.architecture: BERT encoder compressor, blockwise projection of blocks of xi token states to one embedding

other.setting: top-5 concatenated, truncated to 512 tokens, 128 compressed tokens (~x4)

models.name: xRAG-7b and xRAG Mixtral-8x7B
models.architecture: SFR 7B ranking model as compressor, linear projection, frozen decoder

other.setting: top-1 context, one embedding (x128), their stopping criteria

training.objective: Pretraining: auto-encoding (recover input tokens from context embeddings) and language modelling from context embeddings (continue X_B given compressed X_A), sampled with equal probability; fine-tuning: instruction-tuning next-token loss on target response only given compressed contexts and question (Eq. 9)

other.lora: all linear layers, r=16, alpha=32, bias none

inference.prompting: Instruction combining question and context embeddings (Fig 2 'Model Prompt'); [SEP] between passages' embeddings
inference.retrieval: SPLADE-v3, rerank top-50 with DeBERTa-v3, top-5 passages as context in all experiments

other.efficiency_measurement: single A100 40GB, batch size 16 (max that fits), half precision, PyTorch inference mode, torch profiler, first warm-up batch discarded; compression cost on single A100 80GB

limits: Only a 7B model (Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2) tested for compute reasons; no Llama-70B or similar.
Only 5 passages used; gains with many more documents not tested.
Only English QA tasks evaluated; no other tasks or multilingual data.
Baselines use frozen decoders and single contexts (AutoCompressor, xRAG top-1) so comparison mixes tuning regime with method; authors argue they sit between zero-shot and full tuning.
Efficiency measured only on NQ with batch 16; no seeds or variance reported.
Text and tables disagree on rates (xi=1 in 4.1 vs xi=4 in tables); FineWeb subset described as 10 million tokens vs 10m samples; Table 6 COCOM xi=128 NQ 0.519 vs Table 2 0.511.
Higher compression degrades auto-encoding sharply, especially COCOM decoder-based compressor.

terms.definition: a smaller set of embeddings {e1..ek}, k<<n, each in R^d with d the LLM hidden dimension, produced by the compressor from n context tokens
number of context embeddings per context is ceil(n/xi)
